name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained. Common indicators include many failed authentication events from a single source IP targeting one or more accounts within a short time window.
indicators: Multiple failed logins from single IP
High request velocity on /login
HTTP 401 response flood
remediation: Enforce IP rate limiting, account lockout thresholds, and require multi-factor authentication (MFA).

name: Credential Stuffing
description: Adversaries may use credentials obtained from breach dumps to authenticate across multiple accounts using automated bot networks distributed across diverse IP addresses.
indicators: Distributed failed logins from multiple distinct IPs
1-2 attempts per IP across many usernames
Bot user agents
remediation: Deploy bot mitigation, CAPTCHA on login endpoints, and leaked credential detection.

name: Network Service Discovery / Port Scanning
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts. Port scan detection: many distinct destination port connections or endpoint probes from one source IP in a short interval.
indicators: Connections across wide port ranges (21, 22, 80, 443, 3306, 8080)
Scanner user agents (nmap, masscan, zgrab)
Rapid sequential SYN packets
remediation: Block scanning source IP at firewall, disable unnecessary listening services, and implement IDS/IPS port scan alarms.

name: SQL Injection (SQLi)
description: Adversaries may insert malicious SQL statements into web entry fields (e.g. UNION SELECT, OR 1=1, DROP TABLE) to execute arbitrary database commands, extract sensitive data, or bypass authentication.
indicators: SQL meta-characters in URL parameters or POST bodies
Database error messages in HTTP 500 responses
UNION, SELECT, or sleep() payloads
remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements, validate input schemas, and deploy Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules.

name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Adversaries may inject malicious client-side scripts into web applications to execute in the victim browser session, stealing session cookies or redirecting users.
indicators: <script>, javascript:, onerror=, alert() payloads in query strings or form submissions
Reflected script tags in responses
remediation: Implement contextual HTML/JS output encoding, Content Security Policy (CSP), and input sanitization.

name: Suspicious PowerShell Execution
description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell to execute commands, download payloads, and execute scripts in memory using flags like -EncodedCommand, -ExecutionPolicy Bypass, -NoProfile, and -WindowStyle Hidden.
indicators: powershell.exe with -enc / -nop / -w hidden / IEX DownloadString
Base64 encoded command arguments
Unusual child processes of Office or Web servers
remediation: Enable Constrained Language Mode, enforce PowerShell Script Block Logging (EID 4104), and restrict script execution policies.

name: Command Injection
description: Adversaries may execute unauthorized shell commands on the host operating system by appending shell separators (; && | `) to unsanitized application inputs.
indicators: Shell delimiters (; | ` &) followed by whoami, id, cat /etc/passwd, curl, or nc in HTTP requests
Unusual spawning of cmd.exe or /bin/sh by web processes
remediation: Avoid passing input directly to shell execution functions, use safe subprocess APIs with explicit argument vectors.

name: Valid Accounts / Suspicious Authentication
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing valid accounts. Suspicious indicators include logins from anomalous geographic regions, outside standard working hours, or without MFA.
indicators: Successful login from uncharacteristic ASN or country
First-time device login for critical service accounts
Logins outside business hours
remediation: Implement conditional access policies, user behavior analytics (UEBA), and mandatory MFA.

name: Impossible Travel / Geolocation Anomaly
description: Adversaries authenticate using compromised credentials from a geographic location physically impossible to reach given the time elapsed since the previous legitimate user login.
indicators: Consecutive logins for the same user within minutes from distant countries (e.g. US then Russia)
Vastly different source IP subnets
remediation: Enforce real-time velocity checks and trigger automatic session invalidation upon anomalous geolocation hops.

name: Account Takeover (ATO)
description: Adversaries take full control of a legitimate account through password reset hijacking, session hijacking, or credential reuse, followed immediately by security setting alterations.
indicators: Successful authentication followed immediately by email/password changes or MFA device resets
Privilege escalation attempts post-login
remediation: Require re-authentication / step-up verification for critical security profile modifications.

name: Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities or configuration weaknesses to escalate privileges from a standard unprivileged user to Administrator / root / SYSTEM.
indicators: Sudo invocation failures followed by root execution
Token manipulation (SeDebugPrivilege / SeImpersonatePrivilege)
Exploitation of SUID binaries or vulnerable kernel drivers
remediation: Apply latest security patches, enforce principle of least privilege, and monitor sudoers / token changes.

name: Data Exfiltration
description: Adversaries steal sensitive data by transmitting it over an outbound communication channel, DNS tunneling, cloud storage uploads, or encrypted staging endpoints.
indicators: Abnormal outbound data transfer volumes (gigabytes/terabytes to external IPs)
Large HTTP POST or PUT requests to unknown external domains
Unusual DNS query lengths (DNS tunneling)
remediation: Implement Data Loss Prevention (DLP), restrict egress bandwidth and unauthorized cloud upload destinations.

name: Network Denial of Service / DDoS
description: Adversaries perform volumetric network or application-layer DoS attacks to degrade or disrupt service availability to legitimate users.
indicators: Massive spike in HTTP request rates (thousands per minute)
TCP SYN / UDP / ICMP flood signatures
Server timeout (HTTP 502/504) spikes
remediation: Deploy DDoS mitigation reverse proxies (Cloudflare/AWS Shield), configure rate limiting, and use connection throttling.

name: Lateral Movement (SMB/WinRM/SSH)
description: Adversaries move through an internal network by establishing remote connections via SMB (psexec), SSH, RDP, or WinRM using stolen credentials or pass-the-hash.
indicators: Rapid consecutive internal connections from one workstation to multiple database or domain controller hosts (port 445, 3389, 5985, 22)
Service installation events (Event ID 7045)
remediation: Enforce network micro-segmentation, disable SMBv1, and block lateral workstation-to-workstation traffic.

name: Phishing Indicators
description: Adversaries send spearphishing emails containing malicious attachments or deceptive links leading to credential harvesting pages.
indicators: Outbound clicks to newly registered suspicious domains
Email gateway SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures with macro-enabled document attachments
High bounce rates on marketing email spoofing
remediation: Deploy email security filters, enforce DMARC reject policies, and conduct continuous security awareness training.

name: Active Reconnaissance
description: Adversaries execute automated scanning tools to map network perimeters, discover vulnerable endpoints, and catalog web frameworks.
indicators: High volume probes targeting sensitive paths (/.env, /wp-admin, /phpmyadmin, /.git/config, /server-status)
Security scanner signatures (Nikto, DirBuster, Nuclei)
remediation: Hide server identification headers, block unauthenticated access to administrative assets, and feed scanning IPs into dynamic blocklists.

name: Persistence via Scheduled Tasks / Cron
description: Adversaries configure scheduled tasks, systemd services, or cron jobs to maintain recurring execution and survive system reboots.
indicators: Creation of new Windows Scheduled Tasks (schtasks /create) or additions to /etc/cron.* by non-admin processes
Hidden task registry keys
remediation: Audit cron and scheduled task modifications, enforce file integrity monitoring (FIM), and restrict task scheduling privileges.

name: Malware Activity / C2 Beaconing
description: Malicious binaries or scripts executing on host systems communicating regularly with Command and Control (C2) infrastructure.
indicators: Periodic beaconing intervals to unknown external IPs
Known malicious file hashes (MD5/SHA256)
Process injection into explorer.exe or svchost.exe
remediation: Isolate infected endpoints immediately, terminate malicious processes, quarantine files, and block C2 IP/domain indicators.

name: Ransomware Activity / Data Encryption
description: Adversaries encrypt files on target systems and delete volume shadow copies (vssadmin delete shadows) to interrupt business operations and extort ransom.
indicators: High-velocity file modification/renaming with custom extensions (.locked, .enc)
Execution of vssadmin.exe or bcdedit to disable recovery
Ransom note generation (HOW_TO_RECOVER.txt)
remediation: Immediately sever network connectivity of affected hosts, restore from isolated offline backups, and engage incident response.

name: Kerberoasting
description: Adversaries request Service Principal Name (SPN) Kerberos service tickets (TGS) for domain accounts and crack the password hashes offline.
indicators: Spike in Kerberos TGS-REQ requests using RC4 encryption (Event ID 4769) for multiple SPNs from a single user
remediation: Enforce AES encryption for Kerberos, use 25+ character complex passwords for service accounts or migrate to Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).

name: Path Traversal / File Discovery
description: Adversaries utilize directory traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e%2f) to access files and directories stored outside the web root folder.
indicators: ../, %252e%252e%252f, or /etc/passwd in URL path parameters
Attempts to retrieve sensitive configuration or system files
remediation: Sanitize user-supplied file paths, use chroot jail / hardened containerization, and restrict filesystem permissions.

name: Insider Threat / Anomalous Data Access
description: Authorized internal employees or service accounts abusing legitimate privileges to access and extract sensitive files outside normal job scope.
indicators: Access to thousands of customer records / proprietary source code by employee during off-hours or right after resignation notice
Mass downloads to USB/cloud
remediation: Implement Data Loss Prevention (DLP), role-based file access controls, and User Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA).
